Severe weather could cause home and business flooding, building damage, power cuts, and travel disruptions to bus and train services.
July was the driest month on record since 1836 in England and Wales, leaving 70 per cent of those regions in a drought.
Temperatures are expected to reach 26C in London on Thursday, with further changeable weather and above-average rainfall forecast through early September.

title: Russia threatens to attack British factories
author: Joe Barnes; Emily Blumenthal
content:
![John Healey (centre), the former defence secretary, visited a Storm Shadow factory in 2025](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/world-news/2026/08/25/TELEMMGLPICT000431868740_17876263260610_trans_NvBQzQNjv4Bq0alm3aadMyiSD4zlvtFVwUe9oCfNM2DaBAYFZvU1law.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
![John Healey (centre), the former defence secretary, visited a Storm Shadow factory in 2025](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/world-news/2026/08/25/TELEMMGLPICT000431868740_17876263260610_trans_NvBQzQNjv4Bq0alm3aadMyiSD4zlvtFVwUe9oCfNM2DaBAYFZvU1law.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
Russia has threatened to attack British factories after the UK gave Ukraine the blueprints to build its own Storm Shadow missiles.
Andrei Fedorov, a powerful adviser to Vladimir Putin, said Moscow would not “100 per cent exclude” the possibility of “semi-military action” against the manufacturers supplying drone and missile components to Kyiv.
Western intelligence sources told The Telegraph that Russia had already launched a fresh wave of covert attacks against European armament factories.
Mr Fedorov’s intervention on Monday escalated the war of words between London and Moscow over British support for Ukraine.
Earlier that day, the Kremlin had accused Andy Burnham of “adding fuel to the fire” of war by sharing the blueprints with Ukraine. The Prime Minister had replied: “Who started the fire? That’s the question, isn’t it?”
Mr Fedorov made the comments during an appearance on the BBC’s Newsnight after Mr Burnham had visited Kyiv for the first time as Prime Minister and condemned Russia’s “outrageous” threats against Britain.
Although Mr Fedorov did not explicitly say how Moscow would attack, he suggested that a producer of drones or Storm Shadow missile components could be targeted in a cyber-attack by “unknown sources”.
“There might be different political steps and I cannot exclude 100 per cent that there might be some semi-military, for example,” he said.
He then made the threat against British factories, explaining that “semi-military” action meant that “something might happen with enterprises, with the factories which are producing drones for Ukraine”.
“They could be attacked, not by Russia, but by ... from unknown sources,” Mr Fedorov said.
![Russia condemned the decision to share intelligence on Storm Shadow missiles as 'adding fuel to the fire' of the war](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/world-news/2026/08/25/TELEMMGLPICT000393745947_17876258720670_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqpVlberWd9EgFPZtcLiMQf0Rf_Wk3V23H2268P_XkPxc.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
During the Newsnight interview, he said the Prime Minister’s Storm Shadow decision was considered by Moscow to be “direct military involvement” in the war, which he claimed had moved “beyond Ukrainian borders”.
The vulnerability of British industry to cyber-attacks by malign actors has recently come to the fore, with The Telegraph revealing on Saturday that hackers linked to the Iranian regime had shut down a power plant for four days.
Moscow last week threatened unspecified consequences in response to reports that Ukrainian forces had used British-built drones to hit targets on Russian soil.
Russia insisted Britain would pay a “higher price” for its support to Kyiv.
![Remnants of a Storm Shadow missile that was allegedly shot down by Russia](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/world-news/2026/08/25/TELEMMGLPICT000384770231_17876526716700_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqvVgMHbu0goG9Twzt2K1THx5Ok3L2WDlGscgZPW2VLl0.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
However, repeated Russian threats and sabotage operations have so far failed to deter Britain from providing military and intelligence support to Ukraine, and the two countries have only increased their co-operation.
During Mr Burnham’s trip, Ukraine handed over a “goldmine” of intelligence to protect Britain from Russian spies and saboteurs.
Britain is the first country to be given access to Kyiv’s large “Avenger” labs repository, containing millions of images of Russian tanks, air defences, troops, drones and artillery systems from the war.
The data will be used to train technology at British bases to help detect saboteurs and spies trying to gain access to military secrets or sites.
Mr Burnham chaired his first Coalition of the Willing meeting, with France’s Emmanuel Macron and Germany’s Friedrich Merz while in Kyiv.
Mr Macron told the meeting that a string of deadly attacks on Ukrainian cities in recent weeks had shown that allies needed to step up deliveries of interceptors.
Mr Burnham is expected to travel to the US next month to lobby Donald Trump. The US president has not yet given Ukraine the licence to produce Patriot interceptors, as Moscow takes advantage of Kyiv’s dwindling stockpile with deadly ballistic missile bombardments.
Russia has also launched a broader destabilisation campaign across Europe. Western intelligence sources found that Moscow had been behind a series of attacks on European armaments factories.
In recent weeks factories producing drones and ammunition for Ukraine in Italy, Bulgaria and Estonia have been hit by yet-to-be-explained fires and explosions.
The Kremlin has recruited local gang members for the sabotage operations, which the sources believed were designed to fall just short of activating Article 5, Nato’s mutual defence clause.
Mr Fedorov said Britain’s membership of the alliance increased the risk of a Russian attack.
The Slovak authorities revealed on Tuesday that they had foiled a sabotage attack on a factory in the east of the country.
The country’s intelligence services and organised crime police prevented an arson attack on part of the factory where drones are produced, according to SME, the Slovak newspaper.
It is understood that three foreign citizens had been planning the attack, with two arrested in Slovakia and a third detained in Germany on a European arrest warrant.
Investigators uncovered “a large amount of incendiary mixture, tools, mobile phones, an action camera and a hand-drawn plan of the building”, SME reported.
The Slovak authorities did not accuse Russia, but the use of foreign nationals and the attempt to sabotage defence assets in an EU country are both hallmarks of Putin’s hybrid war on Nato.
summary: Russia has threatened potential semi-military or cyber attacks against British factories supplying drone and missile components to Ukraine after the UK shared Storm Shadow blueprints with Kyiv. Andrei Fedorov, an adviser to Vladimir Putin, claimed Moscow views this decision as direct military involvement. Meanwhile, Western intelligence sources indicate that Russia is already conducting covert attacks and sabotage operations against European armament factories.
key_points: Andrei Fedorov stated that Russia could target British factories producing drones or missile components through cyber-attacks or semi-military actions by unknown sources.
The Kremlin criticized the UK's decision to share Storm Shadow blueprints with Ukraine, labeling it as direct military involvement in the war.
Western intelligence sources revealed that Russia has launched a fresh wave of covert attacks and sabotage against European armament factories in Italy, Bulgaria, and Estonia.
Slovak and German authorities recently foiled a planned arson attack on a drone-producing factory in Slovakia and detained foreign suspects.
Despite Russian threats and sabotage, Britain and Ukraine have increased their cooperation, with Kyiv sharing intelligence to help protect the UK from Russian spies.

title: Met Office thunderstorm warning issued across large parts of UK
author: Bryony Gooch
content:
Thunderstorm warnings have been issued across parts of the country as the Met Office warns of flooding and disruption.
Yellow warnings for storms will be in place across the West and East Midlands, as well as the North West, South East, South West and east of England, and parts of Wales.
The alerts will be in force in England and Wales from 3am until 10pm on Wednesday, and 6am until 10pm on Thursday.
The Met Office warned there is a “small risk of flooding and disruption from thunderstorms” with the potential for power cuts after a summer of record-breaking dry conditions.
![A thunderstorm warning is in place across England and Wales](https://static.independent.co.uk/2026/08/25/8/59/Screenshot-2026-08-25-at-09-50-26.png)
A band of heavy showers and thunderstorms is expected to move northwards on Wednesday morning, the forecaster warned, adding an intense downpour of 20 to 30mm of rain could fall in less than an hour.
Some spots could see 40 to 50mm in two to three hours, leading to some surface water flooding, with the possibility of large hail and frequent lightning.
These showers and thunderstorms are expected to drift northwards and ease during the evening.
On Thursday, another band of thunderstorms and heavy rain is expected to move slowly across England and Wales. The Met Office said that 20 to 30mm of rainfall is expected to accumulate in three hours across the affected areas, and up to 50mm in 12 hours can be expected in places.
![Thunderstorms will return on Thursday](https://static.independent.co.uk/2026/08/25/10/51/Screenshot-2026-08-25-at-11-14-59.png)
There is a small chance that some places may see more than 50mm in three hours and more than 75mm through 12 hours, especially over east-facing high ground. Lightning and hail of 1-2cm will also be hazardous, the forecaster warned.
The Met Office warned of a slight chance that power cuts could occur, impacting homes and businesses which could be flooded quickly. Buildings could face damage from floodwater, lightning strikes or hail. Flooding and lightning could cause delays and cancellations to train and bus services.
The risk of spray and sudden flooding could also lead to road closures and difficult driving conditions.
Met Office deputy chief forecaster Mark Sidaway attributed the unsettled weather to warmer and more humid air moving north across the UK.
![Rain is expected across parts of the country on Wednesday](https://static.independent.co.uk/2026/08/25/9/51/Screenshot-2026-08-25-at-10-02-22.png)
“While many areas will see dry and increasingly warm conditions at the start of the week, attention is turning to the potential for heavy rain and thunderstorms from Wednesday onwards,” he said.
“As warmer and more humid air moves north across the UK, there is an increasing likelihood of some heavy rain developing. Some places could see 20 to 30mm of rain in just a few hours, while there is also the potential for higher totals where thunderstorms repeatedly affect the same locations.
“The detail of which areas will see the heaviest rainfall is still uncertain, so stay up to date with the forecast this week to keep updated on the increasing risk of impactful weather during the latter part of the week.”
By Thursday, a band of heavy and thundery rain is expected to move northwards through England and Wales slowly, which could lead to substantial rainfall totals.
The incoming downpour comes as England and Wales are expected to record one of the driest summers on record. Almost three-quarters of England is designated as under drought, as is the entirety of Wales.
Scientists previously warned that a heavy downpour could cause more harm than good following the dry and hot summer, as it could lead to flash flooding in parts of the country.
The Environment Agency flood forecast for the next five days suggests that local flooding from surface water is “possible more widely on Wednesday”, which could bring a deluge to land, roads and some properties.
summary: The Met Office has issued yellow thunderstorm warnings for large parts of England and Wales covering Wednesday and Thursday. The severe weather follows a record-breaking dry summer and could bring heavy downpours, surface water flooding, power cuts, and travel disruptions. Warmer and more humid air moving north across the UK is driving the unsettled conditions.
key_points: Yellow thunderstorm warnings are in place from 3am Wednesday until 10pm Thursday across parts of England and Wales.
Rainfall totals could reach up to 50mm in a few hours, with some isolated areas potentially seeing over 75mm.
The Met Office warned of potential risks including flash flooding, power cuts, lightning strikes, hail, and travel delays.
The incoming storms follow a summer of record-breaking dry conditions where almost three-quarters of England and all of Wales are under drought.

title: Man stabbed to death at Brent Civic Centre in Wembley
author: Share Save Add as preferred
content:
Man stabbed to death at council headquarters
![Google  Brent Civic Centre  in Wembley](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/news/480/cpsprodpb/a605/live/33d7fef0-a099-11f1-8a1f-314a01485cf4.jpg.webp) Google
A young man has died after being stabbed in a building housing Brent Council's headquarters and a library.
Emergency services were called at about 14:30 BST to Brent Civic Centre, near Wembley Stadium in north-west London, where the victim was pronounced dead at the scene.
The Met Police said he was believed to be a teenage boy or man in his early 20s.
No arrests have been made and officers are making urgent inquiries to identify and trace those responsible, the Met said.
![Satellite map of Wembley in northwest London showing the area around Wembley Stadium and Brent Civic Centre. Wembley Stadium is labelled near the bottom centre, and Wembley Park Underground station is marked to the north. A red callout box labelled “Stabbing at Brent Civic Centre” points to a highlighted building just northwest of the stadium. An inset map of London in the top left shows Wembley’s location within the city. Distance scales of 100 metres and 500 feet appear in the bottom right.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/news/480/cpsprodpb/1a3f/live/c04aae40-a09f-11f1-a291-b542ee92de7c.png.webp)
Councillor Muhammed Butt, leader of Brent Council, said: "Brent has been shaken by an appalling and deeply tragic incident at the Civic Centre, in which a person has lost their life.
"Our thoughts are first and foremost with the victim, their family and loved ones, as well as the staff, residents and visitors who witnessed what happened.
"The Civic Centre has been evacuated and will remain closed until further notice. I would urge people to avoid the area and allow the police and emergency services to carry out their work.
"There is an active police investigation under way - please do not speculate or repeat any unverified claims online.
"We are working closely with the Metropolitan Police and will provide further updates as soon as we are able."
'Stop-and-search powers'
Supt Chris Clarke, the Met's lead for emergency response policing in the area, said: "This is an awful incident, in which someone has tragically lost their life. We are working to urgently identify the victim and inform his next of kin as soon as possible.
"We recognise the concern this incident will cause within the local community and are committed to keeping residents informed as our enquiries progress.
"In light of the incident, we have authorised additional stop-and-search powers to help prevent further violence, support our investigation, and keep people safe.
"There will be an increased police presence in and around the area in the coming hours while our officers continue their investigation."
A London Ambulance spokesperson said: "We were called at 14:25 BST today to reports of a stabbing at Brent Civic Centre, Wembley.
"We sent an ambulance crew, paramedics in fast-response cars and an incident response officer. We also dispatched London's Air Ambulance.
"Sadly, despite the best efforts of our crews, a patient was pronounced dead at the scene."
Engineers Way is closed between Empire Way and Exhibition Way, with the 92 and 440 bus routes affected.
summary: A young man was stabbed to death at the Brent Civic Centre in Wembley, which houses the council headquarters and a library. Emergency services responded to the scene at around 14:30 BST, but the victim was pronounced dead. No arrests have been made, and police have launched an active investigation while authorizing additional stop-and-search powers in the area.
key_points: A young man was killed in a stabbing at Brent Civic Centre in north-west London.
Emergency services, including the air ambulance, responded to the incident at about 14:30 BST.
No arrests have been made as police conduct urgent inquiries.
Brent Civic Centre has been evacuated and closed until further notice.
Police have authorised additional stop-and-search powers and increased their presence in the area.

title: Manhunt after young man stabbed to death at London council HQ
author: Matt Watts; Megan Howe
content:
![Add Evening Standard as a preferred source](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/google_preferred_source_badge_dark.png?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
![](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/25/16/31/01M0WWHQ7V4QQJSSCPHPXXPEPH.jpg?trim=103,0,105,0&quality=75&auto=webp&width=1000)
![WEST END FINAL](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/newsletters/newsletter_we_final_embed_desktop.png)
A young man has died following a stabbing in broad daylight inside a council headquarters and library in north London.
Officers rushed to Brent Civic Centre, home to Brent Council, on Engineers Way, at around 2.30pm today following reports of a stabbing.
Upon arrival, officers found the victim, believed to be a teenage boy or man in his early 20s, suffering from stab wounds.
Read More
Despite the efforts of paramedics, the young man was sadly pronounced dead at the scene.
Some staff, residents and visitors saw the fatal attack take place, with reports suggesting the incident took place in the library.
No arrests have yet been made and officers are making urgent enquiries to identify and trace those responsible.
Officers cordoned off the Brent Civic Centre, near Wembley Stadium after the incident. Around 15 emergency vehicles could be seen stationed outside.
Video footage shows a large emergency presence at the scene, as passersby and members of staff gather around the entrance.
One eyewitness wrote on social media: “I was at the exact same place where the stabbing happened and had gone up to the first floor about ten minutes earlier.
“A staff member walked into the meeting room and told us to evacuate because someone had been stabbed. What I witnessed on the way down was unreal.”
Following the incident, a Section 60 order has been authorised, granting officers enhanced powers to stop and search people and vehicles, Met Police said.
This applies to the Wembley Park, Barnhill, Tokyngton, Stonebridge, Roundwood, Dollis Hill, Willesden and Welsh Harp ward areas of Brent.
![The London Air Ambulance landing at the scene outside Brent Civic Centre](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/25/16/19/HQk2d2bWEAAQjcZ.jpeg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
Superintendent Chris Clarke, lead for emergency response policing in the area, said: “This is an awful incident, in which someone has tragically lost their life. We are working to urgently identify the victim and inform his next-of-kin as soon as possible.
“An investigation is underway to establish exactly what has taken place and trace those responsible. We recognise the concern this incident will cause within the local community and are committed to keeping residents informed as our enquiries progress.
“In light of the incident, we have authorised additional stop and search powers to help prevent further violence, support our investigation, and keep people safe.
“There will be an increased police presence in and around the area in the coming hours while our officers continue their investigation.”
![](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/25/17/01M0WWHMEPD1X9135BTNSEAGN9.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
There is not believed to be a wider threat to the community, nor is the incident believed to be terror-related.
An LAS spokesperson said: “We were called at 2:25pm to reports of a stabbing at Brent Civic Centre, Wembley, HA9.
“We sent an ambulance crew, paramedics in fast response cars and an incident response officer.
“We also dispatched London’s Air Ambulance.
“Sadly, despite the best efforts of our crews, a patient was pronounced dead at the scene”.
Commenting on the incident this afternoon, Councillor Muhammed Butt, Leader of Brent Council, said: “Today, Brent has been shaken by an appalling and deeply tragic incident at the Civic Centre, in which a person has lost their life.
“Our thoughts are first and foremost with the victim, their family and loved ones, as well as the staff, residents and visitors who witnessed what happened.
![](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/25/16/28/HQk87JNWMAAqUq1.jpeg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
“The Civic Centre has been evacuated and will remain closed until further notice. I would urge people to avoid the area and allow the police and emergency services to carry out their work.
“There is an active police investigation underway - please do not speculate or repeat any unverified claims online.
“We are working closely with the Metropolitan Police and will provide further updates as soon as we are able.
“I want to express my sincere thanks to the police, paramedics and emergency services for their swift response, and to our staff for the professionalism, compassion and calm they have shown today in the most difficult of circumstances.”
Brent Councillor Anton Georgiu wrote on X: “I am disturbed and saddened by this news. My heart goes out to the victim and their loved ones. Thinking also of staff and visitors to @BrentCouncil who witnessed what happened today.”
A spokesperson for the Brent Conservatives said: “We are shocked and deeply saddened by the fatal stabbing at Brent Civic Centre today. Our thoughts and deepest sympathies are with the victim’s family and loved ones and everyone affected by this tragedy. We thank the emergency services for their response.”
Anybody with information is urged to call 101, quoting reference 4032/25AUG.
summary: A young man was fatally stabbed in broad daylight inside the Brent Civic Centre in north London, prompting a major emergency response and an active police manhunt. Despite the efforts of paramedics and the London Air Ambulance, the victim was pronounced dead at the scene. No arrests have been made, and police have authorized enhanced stop and search powers under a Section 60 order in several Brent wards.
key_points: A young man was stabbed to death inside the Brent Civic Centre, which houses Brent Council headquarters and a library.
Police and emergency services responded to the scene at around 2.30pm, but the victim was pronounced dead despite medical efforts.
No arrests have been made yet, and officers are conducting urgent enquiries to trace those responsible.
A Section 60 order granting enhanced stop and search powers has been authorized across multiple Brent ward areas.
Authorities confirmed the incident is not believed to be terror-related and there is no wider threat to the community.

title: Young man stabbed to death at London council building
author: Cameron Henderson
content:
![Emergency services at the Brent Civic Centre](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/news/2026/08/25/TELEMMGLPICT000499510540_17876702486101_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqyuLFFzXshuGqnr8zPdDWXhbQKbwj1ZsnNMhuR7O6ySI.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
![Emergency services at the Brent Civic Centre](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/news/2026/08/25/TELEMMGLPICT000499510540_17876702486101_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqyuLFFzXshuGqnr8zPdDWXhbQKbwj1ZsnNMhuR7O6ySI.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
A young man has been stabbed to death in a building which houses the headquarters of a London council.
Emergency services were at the scene of the stabbing at Brent Civic Centre in Wembley, north-west London, on Tuesday.
Images on social media showed police cars, paramedics and an air ambulance in the area.
A cordon is in place at the scene and the building has been evacuated.
Ruqiya, 39, from Wembley, who witnessed some of the incident, told The Telegraph: “A boy tried to fight another boy [outside the library].
“He had a knife and he started to stab. The other boy ran away and he ran with him. Then he ran inside the Brent Civic Centre. He went inside with him and then fell down.”
Another witness said: “I was in the library on the mezzanine level when it happened, and from what I could see from the balcony there was somebody on the floor and splatters of blood.”
![A police cordon was set up outside Brent Civic Centre, which houses the Brent council headquarters](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/news/2026/08/25/TELEMMGLPICT000499508069_17876706938610_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqRo0U4xU-30oDveS4pXV-Vv4Xpit_DMGvdp2n7FDd82k.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
Another wrote: “I was at the same place where the stabbing happened and had gone up to the first floor about 10 minutes earlier.
“A staff member walked into the meeting room and told us to evacuate because someone had been stabbed. What I witnessed on the way down was unreal.”
A statement on the council website read: “The Brent Civic Centre and Wembley Library are currently closed due to an ongoing incident. Please avoid visiting the building at this time. We’ll share updates as soon as we can.”
A London Ambulance Service spokesman said: “We were called at 2.25pm on Aug 25 to reports of a stabbing at Brent Civic Centre, Wembley, HA9.
“We sent an ambulance crew, paramedics in fast response cars and an incident response officer. We also dispatched London’s Air Ambulance. Sadly, despite the best efforts of our crews, a patient was pronounced dead at the scene.”
![Police and the ambulance service at the scene in Brent](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/news/2026/08/25/TELEMMGLPICT000499510542_17876702721600_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqTEeXHR7TXuV8gaTwxPVJbMPQg023f4d5cp0FsANlXbI.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
Brent Civic Centre is a nine-storey building, which houses the headquarters of Brent council as well as private office buildings. More than 2,000 staff work in the building, which also hosts surgeries by local politicians.
Muhammed Butt, the leader of Brent council, said: “Today, Brent has been shaken by an appalling and deeply tragic incident at the Civic Centre, in which a person has lost their life.
“Our thoughts are first and foremost with the victim, their family and loved ones, as well as the staff, residents and visitors who witnessed what happened.
“The Civic Centre has been evacuated and will remain closed until further notice. I would urge people to avoid the area and allow the police and emergency services to carry out their work.”
Mr Butt added: “There is an active police investigation under way – please do not speculate or repeat any unverified claims online. We are working closely with the Metropolitan Police and will provide further updates as soon as we are able.
“I want to express my sincere thanks to the police, paramedics and emergency services for their swift response, and to our staff for the professionalism, compassion and calm they have shown today in the most difficult of circumstances.”
The Metropolitan Police has been contacted for comment.
summary: A young man was stabbed to death at the Brent Civic Centre in north-west London on Tuesday. Emergency services, including an air ambulance, responded to the scene, but the victim was pronounced dead despite their efforts. The building, which houses the Brent council headquarters and Wembley Library, was evacuated and closed following the incident.
key_points: A young man was stabbed to death at the Brent Civic Centre in Wembley.
Emergency services including police, paramedics, and an air ambulance responded at approximately 2:25pm on August 25.
The building, which houses Brent council headquarters and Wembley Library, was evacuated and closed.
Witnesses reported seeing a fight involving a knife before the victim collapsed inside the building.
Brent council leader Muhammed Butt released a statement expressing condolences and urging the public to avoid the area.

title: Anglesey: Arrest after taxi driven wrong way down A55 dual carriageway
author: Catriona Aitken
content:
![Police vehicles and officers in high-vis sutrrounding a grey van with taxi branding.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1800/cpsprodpb/f1fa/live/c1f75430-a09c-11f1-8a1f-314a01485cf4.jpg)
Police stopped the vehicle while it was travelling the wrong way down the A55 on Anglesey
- Published
A man has been arrested after a taxi knocked a cyclist off their bike and then drove the wrong way down a dual carriageway.
Officers intervened on the A55 westbound on Anglesey on Monday evening, temporarily closing the road while they stopped the taxi between Rhosneigr and Rhostrehewfa.
North Wales Police said it had received a report of a taxi being stolen from Holyhead at about 19:30 BST.
Shortly after, the taxi had been involved in a collision with a cyclist on London Road, during which several parked vehicles were also damaged, before entering the A55.
The cyclist was taken to hospital with non-life threatening injuries.
A man was arrested on suspicion of vehicle theft, dangerous driving and failing to provide specimen for analysis. He remained in custody on Tuesday.
Temporary Assistant Chief Constable Nick Evans said urged anyone with information about or footage of the incident to contact the force.
"It is clear to all of us, particularly in light of the tragic events in Cleveland, just how serious the potential consequences of this incident were," he said.
"I am extremely proud of the courage and professionalism shown by our officers in resolving a highly challenging situation safely.
"I would encourage people not to speculate about the circumstances of the incident or any possible motivations while our investigation remains ongoing."
In a social media post, the owner of the taxi company, Tacsi Zoe, said: "I want to make it absolutely clear that this was not myself or any of my drivers. I was personally caught up in this and, like many others, found the whole situation extremely scary and traumatic.
"A huge thank you to all the police officers involved for their quick response and for bringing the situation to a safe conclusion."
Police said there were no collisions as a result of the vehicle travelling in the wrong direction, but their investigation was ongoing.
summary: A man was arrested after a stolen taxi knocked down a cyclist, damaged parked cars, and was driven the wrong way down the A55 dual carriageway on Anglesey. Police intervened on Monday evening, temporarily closing the road to stop the vehicle between Rhosneigr and Rhostrehewfa. The injured cyclist was taken to hospital with non-life threatening injuries.
key_points: A taxi was reported stolen from Holyhead at about 19:30 BST on Monday.
The vehicle struck a cyclist and damaged several parked vehicles on London Road before entering the A55.
A man was arrested on suspicion of vehicle theft, dangerous driving, and failing to provide a specimen for analysis.
Police confirmed no collisions occurred while the vehicle was traveling the wrong way down the dual carriageway.

title: Burnham hands troubled housebuilder £350m for council housing blitz
author: Tom Haynes
content:
![Andy Burnham](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/business/2026/08/25/TELEMMGLPICT000499433498_17876437110090_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqMQG2G_DL9n2BG-K8dLuv531W1tg313se3he3TeUBMNA.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
![Andy Burnham](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/business/2026/08/25/TELEMMGLPICT000499433498_17876437110090_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqMQG2G_DL9n2BG-K8dLuv531W1tg313se3he3TeUBMNA.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
Andy Burnham has handed an embattled housebuilder £350m to boost his council housebuilding blitz.
Vistry, one of Britain’s biggest housing groups, will receive the cash to build about 3,000 affordable homes under a £10bn government programme to construct 70,000 homes outside London.
The award comes just weeks after Vistry revealed it had plunged to a £30m loss, which had raised fears over its finances.
Shares in the housebuilder have also fallen by more than 70pc from their peak in August 2024, although they soared more than 18pc after the Government announced the funding.
Insurers have also pulled cover, with Allianz Trade warning suppliers earlier this month it was cutting exposure to the group.
Vistry’s main business is building properties for housing associations and councils using public funding, which has paved the way for Mr Burnham’s award.
However, it has struggled in recent years with a downturn in the sector. Greg Fitzgerald, the former chief executive, resigned in March after a string of profit warnings.
Only around 60pc of that money will be earmarked for social rented property, months after Mr Burnham said Labour’s £39bn housing plan should be “dedicated to council homes”.
The rest of the funding will go towards other types of accommodation, including shared ownership schemes and sheltered housing, rather than council housing.
Labour’s plans were criticised as “a sleight of hand” by the Conservatives, who accused the Government of making an “unfunded spending commitment” that would take more than a decade to complete.
Sir James Cleverly, the shadow housing secretary, added that some properties would not be completed for more than 13 years.
He said: “The small print shows homes won’t have to be delivered until 2039.” Under the programme rules, homes must start by March 2036 and be completed by March 2039.
Mr Burnham has argued that the £39bn programme, announced under Sir Keir Starmer’s government, should be “dedicated to council homes”, adding: “Let’s not be coy any more ... I’m saying council homes because control matters.”
But only three councils are among the 33 groups receiving guaranteed funding, with most of the money going to housing associations.
London is also set to receive a further £10bn from the programme as part of Labour’s target to build 300,000 by 2036.
The Government confirmed the full list on Tuesday of 33 groups to receive the initial funding. These include housing associations such as Clarion, Orbit, Places for People and Sanctuary, as well as developers including Vistry and Sage Homes.
Several of the housing providers have faced criticism from the Housing Ombudsman over their treatment of tenants.
Places for People was reprimanded for “severe maladministration” last year after taking around eight months to inspect a home affected by damp and mould and a further seven months to complete repairs. It was ordered to pay £2,100 in compensation.
Clarion, Britain’s biggest housing association, was reprimanded by Michael Gove, the former housing secretary, in 2024 after the Housing Ombudsman found four cases of severe maladministration.
Mr Gove wrote to Clarion’s chief executive after the watchdog uncovered delays, poor communication and failures to act on repairs.
In one case, leaks were left unresolved for five years, while another involved failures to respond properly to damp and mould.
Sage Homes was also ordered to conduct an independent review after the Ombudsman found it had failed to address a resident’s vulnerabilities and safeguarding concerns properly.
The affordable housing announcement came as Reform UK also unveiled plans to increase social housing supply, including allowing housing associations to borrow more and expanding Right to Buy.
The party has said it would prioritise British-born applicants for social housing.
Amy Rees, the Homes England chief executive, said on Tuesday that strong demand for funding showed the sector still backed plans to deliver thousands of social and affordable homes.
She said: “Our team is absolutely focused on working in close collaboration with our partners alongside regional leaders, mayors and the sector to deliver on government policy and ensure this investment supports the creation of high-quality homes and thriving places that people want and need.”
summary: Andy Burnham has awarded £350m to the embattled housebuilder Vistry to construct around 3,000 affordable homes as part of a government housing programme. The funding arrives shortly after Vistry reported a £30m loss, suffered a significant drop in share value from its 2024 peak, and faced insurers pulling cover. Only about 60pc of the allocated money will be directed towards social rented properties, with the remainder supporting shared ownership and sheltered housing.
key_points: Vistry received £350m to build approximately 3,000 affordable homes following recent financial struggles and a £30m loss.
Only about 60pc of the awarded funding is earmarked for social rented property, while the rest goes to shared ownership and sheltered housing.
Conservatives criticized the broader government housing plan, pointing out that programme rules allow homes to be completed as late as March 2039.
The initial funding is being distributed among 33 groups, predominantly housing associations alongside developers like Vistry and Sage Homes.

title: UK weather: Met Office issues yellow weather warnings for thunderstorms
author: Tomasz Schafernaker
content:
![Three women walk under an umbrella during a rainstorm in London](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/924/cpsprodpb/b1a4/live/ab342830-a061-11f1-a8b2-73da9d854f1b.png)
- Published
Yellow weather warnings have been issued by the Met Office as heavy rain and thunderstorms are forecast to break out over parts of the UK later this week.
The warnings span Wednesday and Thursday and include parts of east Wales, the Midlands, northern England, East Anglia and southern England - including London.
It is likely to be the one of the most widespread outbreaks of heavy rain across southern and central parts of the UK this summer.
While good news for regions plagued by drought, significant accumulations could lead to flash flooding where the ground is too dry and hard to absorb the downpours. Lightning, large hail and gusty winds are also possible.
Thunderstorms to fire up on Wednesday morning
The storms, which will drift out of France and move northwards, will be sparked as warm and humid air sets in from the south.
Initially, a few showers are likely to reach Cornwall and the West Country during Tuesday evening, but heavier downpours bringing thunder and lightning are likely to hit later in the night.
The first band of heavy showers may reach the southeast coast of England around midnight, and then cross Greater London before moving northwards into the home counties and East Anglia.
![A map depicting the area covered by a yellow weather warning, which includes Basingstoke and London in the south and Stockport and Sheffield in the north.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/a5a4/live/07794620-a067-11f1-aed2-8d6da8d75094.jpg)
The first yellow weather warning is set to come into force at 03:00 BST on Wednesday and last until 22:00 BST.
Though not all locations in the warning area will experience thunderstorms, flooding is possible in those that do, with 20-30mm of rain possible in less than an hour.
The hardest hit locations could see up to 40-50mm in two to three hours.
Flash flooding is possible in areas where the ground is dry and very hard, making it difficult for rainfall to be absorbed. The most intense downpours could also bring large hail with gusty winds.
During the morning on Wednesday, the storms may spread further north into the Midlands and the Peak District but the forecast becomes less certain in terms of location and intensity.
Thunderstorm and flood threat continues on Thursday
The storms and downpours which will have brought flash flooding and hail are forecast to continue into Thursday.
A second weather warning for thunderstorms will come into force at 06:00 BST and last until 22:00 BST.
Some may become slow moving across the Midlands, Wales and Northern England leading to more flash flooding.
![A Met Office yellow weather warning area for thunderstormswhich shows Cardiff, Bristol and Oxford within the warning area in the south and Liverpool and Leeds in the warning area further north.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/20a8/live/586a4e30-a06c-11f1-aed2-8d6da8d75094.jpg)
Many areas could see 20-30mm of rain in just three hours, with up to 50mm possible in some places.
According to the Met Office, there is also a small chance of considerably higher totals, particularly over east-facing higher ground, where more than 75mm could fall within 12 hours.
Lightning may be frequent and hail of around 1-2cm could fall.
Why are rain and thunderstorms difficult to forecast?
Thunderstorms are notoriously difficult to predict because they can develop very quickly and on a relatively small scale.
Tiny differences in temperature, humidity, wind and atmospheric instability can determine whether a storm forms at all or where it moves.
Forecast models can often identify the risk of thunderstorms across a wider area, but pinpointing precisely where and when an individual storm will strike is very hard.
Even a few kilometres can make the difference between a torrential downpour with thunder and lightning, and somewhere staying completely dry.
summary: The Met Office has issued yellow weather warnings for thunderstorms and heavy rain covering parts of the UK on Wednesday and Thursday. Warm and humid air moving up from France is expected to trigger widespread downpours, bringing risks of flash flooding, lightning, large hail, and gusty winds. Forecasters note that thunderstorms are notoriously difficult to predict precisely due to their localized and fast-developing nature.
key_points: Yellow weather warnings span Wednesday and Thursday across regions including parts of east Wales, the Midlands, northern England, East Anglia, and southern England.
The storms are expected to bring 20-30mm of rain in a short time, with up to 40-50mm possible in the hardest hit locations.
Flash flooding is a significant risk because dry, hard ground struggles to absorb heavy downpours quickly.
Thunderstorms are difficult to forecast accurately because tiny differences in temperature, humidity, and wind determine where they form.

title: Five more arrests in Middlesbrough A66 wrong-way crash investigation
author: Tom MacDougall
content:
![Pictures of the two officers. Both are smiling. PC Blades, left, has stubble and short fair hair. PC Clough also has stubble and short dark hair.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/68ab/live/93348dd0-9f24-11f1-b109-879e35c24276.png)
PC Matthew Blades and PC Tom Clough were killed in a crash near Middlesbrough on Saturday
- Published
Five more people have been arrested in an investigation into a wrong-way crash on the A66 in Middlesbrough which killed seven people, including two police officers.
Cleveland Police said a 16-year-old boy and two men, 18 and 21, were arrested on suspicion of participating in an organised crime group. A 55-year-old man was also arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender and a 23-year-old man on suspicion of making threats to kill.
Two men have also been charged, one for possession of a firearm with intent to endager life, and one with possession with intent to supply class A and class B drugs and possession of criminal property.
All five of the newly arrested men remain in custody.
Twelve arrests had already been made, bringing the total to 17.
PC Tom Clough, 38, and PC Matthew Blades, 37, died in the crash, as did Michael Robert Cahill, 23, Jacob Matusiak, 23, Makai Saddington, 18, Theo Rae, 17, and 17-year-old Cole Robert Worthy.
All seven were killed when a Volkswagen Passat, going the wrong way down the A66 at South Bank, hit a Cleveland Police armed response vehicle heading in the opposite direction at 03:39 BST on Saturday.
The Independent Office for Police Conduct said officers had been pursuing the Passat for almost seven minutes after it was connected to earlier alleged criminal activity, but the pursuit was abandoned 10 seconds before the crash when it turned on to the dual carriageway.
![Five young men in their late teens and early 20s. They all have similar haircuts, with a fringe and faded back and sides. Four of them are gesturing with their fingers. Three of them extend their thumb, index, and pinky fingers - leaving their middle and ring finger tucked down. One points with his index and middle finger whilst holding a Lucozade bottle. They are all dressed in casual clothing.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2560/cpsprodpb/0763/live/9fa0d730-9f34-11f1-a291-b542ee92de7c.jpg)
The five who died in the Passat were Jacob Matusiak, Makai Saddington, Theo Ray, Michael Robert Cahill and Cole Robert Worthy
On Monday, the force said it received several reports of two vehicles "being driven dangerously" on Saturday morning.
The first vehicle, believed to be a Volvo XC60, was seen "ramming properties" in the Middlesbrough area while the second vehicle, a Passat, is believed to have been associated with this activity.
Both vehicles were operating with cloned number plates but were picked up by automated number plate recognition technology.
Nine men and three women, aged between 19 and 61, were arrested across Teesside on Monday over suspicion of a range of offences, including possession of a firearm and being part of an organised crime group.
Two men, have since been charged as part of the investigation.
Watch: Security footage from a house on Lime Road in Middlesbrough appears to show a car being pursued by police vehicles three minutes before the crash
Those previously arrested as part of the investigation are:
- Three men, aged 24, 19 and 35, all held on suspicion of participating in an organised crime group and possession of an offensive weapon. They are in police custody.
- A man, 21, held on suspicion of participating in an organised crime group, possession of an offensive weapon and criminal damage. He has been remanded on recall to prison
- A 30-year-old woman arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender and who is in police custody
- A 20-year-old man arrested on suspicion of threats to cause criminal damage and public order. He remains in custody
- A 26-year-old man was charged with possession with intent to supply class A drugs, as well as the possession of criminal property. He was remanded in custody ahead of his next court hearing
- Another man, 39, and a 47-year-old woman have been released on conditional bail after both being arrested on suspicion of possessing a firearm without a certificate, possession with intent to supply class A and class B drugs, and possession of class C drugs
- An 18-year-old man has been released on unconditional bail after being arrested on suspicion of possessing a firearm without a certificate, possession with intent to supply class A and class B drugs, and possession of class C drugs
- A 61-year-old woman has been released on conditional bail after being arrested on suspicion of possessing a firearm without a certificate
- A 39-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of threats to kill and has been released on conditional bail
Follow BBC Tees on X,, external Facebook, external, Nextdoor and Instagram, external and listen to Radio Tees on BBC Sounds.
summary: Five more people have been arrested in connection with a wrong-way crash on the A66 in Middlesbrough that resulted in the deaths of seven people, including two police officers. The incident occurred when a Volkswagen Passat traveling the wrong way collided with a Cleveland Police armed response vehicle after a police pursuit was abandoned. This brings the total number of arrests in the ongoing investigation to 17.
key_points: Five additional arrests bring the total number of people arrested in the investigation to 17.
The crash killed seven people, including Cleveland Police officers PC Tom Clough and PC Matthew Blades.
The collision happened when a Volkswagen Passat driving the wrong way down the A66 struck a police armed response vehicle.
Police had pursued the Passat for nearly seven minutes before abandoning the chase 10 seconds prior to the crash.

title: Burnham to take Zelenskyy’s pleas for Patriot missiles to Trump – Europe live
author: Taz Ali; Martin Belam; Raphael Boyd
content:
Kremlin accuses Burnham of wanting Ukraine war to continue
Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov has accused Andy Burnham of wanting the conflict in Ukraine to continue, saying the UK prime minister and Finnish president Alexander Stubb belonged to the “party of war”, Russian media reported.
During a visit to Kyiv yesterday, Stubb said he supported Ukraine’s long-range strikes on Russian territory, arguing that they could raise the cost of war for Russia and help force Moscow to the negotiating table.
When asked to respond, Peskov said: “We now see that such escalatory statements have prevailed. Mr Stubb is also a prominent representative of the ‘war party’, along with the British prime minister. They have distinguished themselves over the past few days with such bellicose statements. They want the war to continue.”
A man from Yorkshire is believed to be the first British citizen to die fighting for Russia in its war against Ukraine.
Bradley Townsend, a 33-year-old fisher from Barnsley, left Britain in April to join up with Russian separatists in eastern Donbas to aid in their invasion of Ukraine, despite having no previous combat experience or familiar ties to eastern Europe. Alongside 49-year-old Ben Stimson and 39-year-old Aiden Minnis, Townsend was granted Russian citizenship for joining the country’s military campaign.
He is believed to have been killed by a remote-controlled first-person-view drone near Lyman, a city in Donetsk, on 10 June. He appeared in videos posted to social media by pro-Russian accounts, including one seemingly owned by Stimson, who was jailed in the UK in 2015 prior to Russia’s full scale invasion for travelling to join pro-Russian troops to fight in the region.
Zelenskyy: Ukraine has received a small number of US-made Patriot interceptors
Ukraine has recently received a small number of US-made Patriot interceptors capable of downing Russian ballistic missiles, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Tuesday.
Reuters reports the country also got confirmation of future supplies of the French Crotale surface-to-air missile system. He did not say how many had arrived, or who had supplied them. Zelenskyy was speaking to Ukrainian state broadcaster Suspilne.
Russia rejects French accusations of Moscow carrying out cyberattack campaign
A lot of diplomatic news out of Moscow today, where the Russian foreign ministry has rejected accusations by France that Moscow allegedly conducted a cyberattack campaign against European countries including France, saying Paris was trying to revive the “myth of a ‘Russian threat.’”
Vatican envoy Paul Gallagher met Russian foreign minister Sergei Lavrov in Moscow earlier today, and Reuters has some snap quotes from Pope Leo XIV’s representative following the meeting. He is quoted as saying that “The Ukrainian war must end” and that the pair discussed “avenues for pursuing lasting and just peace in Ukraine”.
In relation to the post on a US military plane landing in Moscow (at 11:23), Reuters reported that the last time a US jet flew to Russia from Europe was in January, when special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner travelled to Moscow to meet Vladimir Putin for peace talks.
Also in Moscow this morning, Vatican envoy Paul Gallagher met Russian foreign minister Sergei Lavrov, stressing the importance of diplomacy and dialogue during what he called a difficult time for international relations, Reuters reports.
Gallagher said the world needed diplomacy more than ever.
Paul Gallagher, Vatican envoy and secretary for relations with states and international organisations of the Holy See, and Russian foreign minister Sergei Lavrov arrive for a meeting in Moscow. Photograph: Ramil Sitdikov/AFP/Getty Images
A US military transport aircraft has landed in Moscow, according to air traffic monitoring data cited by Russia’s Tass news agency.
Data showed the plane departed from Joint Base Andrews near Washington on Sunday, transited Riga in Latvia and landed in Moscow at about 10am local time this morning.
Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov had no information about the Boeing C-17A Globemaster III that landed in Moscow, Tass reported.
There’s scant information available at the moment but we will bring you more as we get it.
Kremlin accuses Burnham of wanting Ukraine war to continue
Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov has accused Andy Burnham of wanting the conflict in Ukraine to continue, saying the UK prime minister and Finnish president Alexander Stubb belonged to the “party of war”, Russian media reported.
During a visit to Kyiv yesterday, Stubb said he supported Ukraine’s long-range strikes on Russian territory, arguing that they could raise the cost of war for Russia and help force Moscow to the negotiating table.
When asked to respond, Peskov said: “We now see that such escalatory statements have prevailed. Mr Stubb is also a prominent representative of the ‘war party’, along with the British prime minister. They have distinguished themselves over the past few days with such bellicose statements. They want the war to continue.”
Perpetrators behind German airport drone bomb 'will pay,' says Merz
We are seeing the first reports of German chancellor Friedrich Merz’s statement this morning ahead of a cabinet meeting in Brandenburg.
He has spoken out for the first time about the attempted drone attack on Leipzig airport earlier this month. As my colleagues Deborah ColeandAndrew Rothreported at the time, a small drone carrying explosives was found at Leipzig/Halle airport, a major cargo and military logistics hub that handles aid shipments to Ukraine. The incident triggered an alarm and forced several flights to be diverted. German police deployed a bomb disposal robot to defuse and destroy the explosive device, which was found in the vicinity of several Ukrainian cargo planes.
German chancellor Friedrich Merz speaks to the media at the start of a two-day cabinet retreat. Photograph: Sean Gallup/EPA
Merz said Germany has “increasingly come into the crosshairs of hybrid attackers” and that perpetrators must face consequences. “They will pay for it,” Merz said, according to the German newspaper Die Welt.
Merz said his government was “working closely with the security authorities” on the matter, and that it will present its findings “shortly”.
Local media, citing security sources, have reported potential Russian involvement in the attempted attack, but Merz did not comment on the possible perpetrators.
At least 35,000 excess deaths recorded in Europe’s back-to-back heatwaves
In other news, at least 35,000 more people died during Europe’s record-breaking heatwaves this summer than would normally be expected, the Guardian’s Europe correspondent Jon Henley reports.
According to provisional national figures, which cover barely half of the continent, excess mortality in three of the EU’s larger countries – Germany, France and Spain – has already exceeded 25,000, as experts warn the toll will rise significantly once August totals are consolidated.
Zelenskyy has been thanking world leaders individually on X for their messages of support on Ukraine’s independence day (35, and counting). Here is his message to King Charles and Queen Camilla:
Warm and sincere Independence Day wishes from His Majesty King Charles III and Her Majesty The Queen are deeply moving and exceptionally meaningful.
I am grateful for the emphasis on Ukraine’s history, rich culture, and unyielding national spirit, as well as the resilience of the Ukrainian people, who continue to defend their homeland and uphold the values that define our state.
The steadfast friendship between Ukraine and the United Kingdom remains an invaluable wellspring of strength for our nation.
We are sincerely grateful for the constant solidarity shown by the British people. Our special bond is built upon our shared commitment to freedom, democracy, and justice.
I wish His Majesty good health and continued success, as well as peace and prosperity for the United Kingdom and its people.”
Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy shakes hands with King Charles at Buckingham Palace on 17 March 2026. Photograph: Aaron Chown/AP
It’s worth reading Zelenskyy’s social media post about Trump in full (particularly the last line). Here is what he wrote on X:
I received warm and heartening congratulations from President Trump on the 35th Anniversary of the Restoration of Ukraine’s Independence:
“Dear Mr. President:
On behalf of the American people, I congratulate you and the citizens of Ukraine on your Independence Day. August 24 is a day to celebrate our enduring friendship built on 35 years of diplomatic relations, a bond that has only deepened since Ukraine gained its independence.
With courageous, brave, and talented people, you have built a great country. As you commemorate this important occasion, know that the United States stands in admiration of your resilient spirit, honors your sacrifices, and remains confident in your future as a sovereign, prosperous nation.
Let us seize this moment to end the conflict and build a durable, lasting peace that unleashes the tremendous potential of Ukraine for generations to come.
Sincerely,
Donald J. Trump”
These words, much like the sound of a Patriot PAC-3 launch, lift our spirits and give hope that lives can be protected from Russia’s savage attacks and that a dignified peace can be achieved. Thank you, President Trump and all Americans, for your support and congratulations!”
Opening summary: Burnham to take Zelenskyy's pleas for Patriot missiles to Trump - report
Hello, and welcome to our Europe live blog. A day after hosting world leaders in Ukraine for the country’s independence day celebrations, president Volodymyr Zelenskyy has taken to social media with a flurry of posts thanking those who sent their best wishes, including Donald Trump.
The Ukrainian president appeared to make a pointed nod to one of his most pressing requests, saying Trump’s message of support lifted spirits “much like the sound of a Patriot PAC-3 launch”. The US Patriot air defence system has been instrumental in protecting Ukraine’s cities from Russian attacks, but stocks are running dangerously low. The shortage has been compounded by the US and Israel’s war on Iran, with Patriot interceptors diverted to defend US bases and regional allies in the Middle East, leaving fewer available for Ukraine as Russia continues to launch waves of ballistic missiles.
In his first international trip as prime minister, Andy Burnham arrived in Kyiv yesterday where he announced the UK government will release the blueprints for British-made components for the Scalp missile, a French version of the UK’s Storm Shadow cruise missile, allowing Ukraine to work with France to produce its own version.
Ukraine’s president Volodymyr Zelenskyy shakes hands with Britain’s prime minister Andy Burnham ahead of their bilateral meeting in Kyiv on Monday.
“Ukraine has been Europe’s protector, not a drain on our security, but the frontline of keeping Europe safe,” Burnham said.
In an interview with Bloomberg, Burnham said he would travel to the New York next month to join European leaders lobbying Trump to supply Ukraine with Patriot missiles. If it goes ahead, it would be his first trip to the US as prime minister.
Burnham said he was “really optimistic” that Ukraine’s interceptor shortage was “fixable”, but added: “There are other players who could help in the mix who we have influence with. It’s probably going to be a solution that involves a lot of layers and a lot of negotiation.”
Also today:
European council president, António Costa, is on his way to Slovakia as part of his annual tour of European capitals. He is scheduled to hold talks in Bratislava with prime minister Robert Fico, who has not been as forthcoming as other European leaders on military aid to Ukraine.
Russia’s foreign minister Sergei Lavrov will host the Vatican’s most senior diplomat, Paul Gallagher, for talks in Moscow. The official Vatican News described the four-day visit as “a mission of dialogue and peace”, but made no mention of whether Ukraine would be on the agenda.
German chancellor Friedrich Merz is back from summer recess and is meeting with his ministers in Brandenburg this morning. He faces a crucial test at the polls next month, with his party under pressure to hold ground against the surging far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD). The AfD has a real chance of taking power in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt on 6 September – one of three state elections taking place this autumn – in what could be a major blow to Merz’s coalition.
summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced during a visit to Kyiv that he will travel to the US next month to lobby President Trump to supply Ukraine with Patriot missiles to address critical interceptor shortages. Meanwhile, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov criticized Burnham and Finnish President Alexander Stubb as belonging to a "party of war" following their support for Ukraine's military strikes. In other developments, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed Ukraine has recently received a small number of US-made Patriot interceptors, and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz vowed consequences following an attempted drone bomb attack at Leipzig airport.
key_points: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham plans to travel to the US to lobby President Trump for Patriot missile supplies for Ukraine.
Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov accused Burnham and Finnish President Alexander Stubb of wanting the war in Ukraine to continue.
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced that Ukraine has received a small number of US-made Patriot interceptors.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz stated that perpetrators of an attempted drone attack at Leipzig airport will face consequences.

title: Minister under fire for paying tribute to A66 joyriders
author: Amy Gibbons
content:
![Anna Turley paid her respects to all seven victims of the collision in her constituency](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/briefs/2026/08/25/TELEMMGLPICT000499441417_17876448403960_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqVoDyJMojtbE029uPw_rygEXTv3igcKmD5Bzd0ykNPxc.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
![Anna Turley paid her respects to all seven victims of the collision in her constituency](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/briefs/2026/08/25/TELEMMGLPICT000499441417_17876448403960_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqVoDyJMojtbE029uPw_rygEXTv3igcKmD5Bzd0ykNPxc.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
A Home Office minister is under fire for paying tribute to five joyriders who died in a crash that killed two police officers.
Anna Turley, the MP for Redcar and border security minister, was accused of putting the two officers “on a par” with the five youths who died in a car travelling in the wrong direction on the A66 near Middlesbrough on Saturday.
Makai Saddington, 18, Theo Rae and Cole Worthy, both 17, and Michael Cahill and Jacob Matusiak, both 23, crashed into the car of Pc Matthew Blades and Pc Tom Clough, killing both officers.
Ms Turley paid her respects to all seven victims of the collision, which was in her constituency.
She wrote on Facebook on Sunday: “This morning I went down to South Bank to lay flowers and pay my respects, on behalf of our whole community, to the seven people whose lives were so tragically cut short yesterday.
“There really are no words for the heartbreak their families, friends and loved ones will be feeling today. May you all rest in peace.”
![Makai Saddington, Theo Rae, Cole Worthy, Michael Cahill and Jacob Matusiak died when they crashed into the police car near Middlesborough](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/briefs/2026/08/25/TELEMMGLPICT000499308373_17876454775871_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqqVzuuqpFlyLIwiB6NTmJwfSVWeZ_vEN7c6bHu2jJnT8.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
Nick Timothy, the shadow justice secretary, said it did not “feel right” for a Home Office minister to honour the lives of the five joyriders, four of whom had 37 convictions between them, along with the police officers.
In a post on X, he said: “Anna Turley is a Home Office minister. She wants to ‘pay her respects to the seven people whose lives were tragically cut short’ in the Middlesbrough crash this weekend.
“I can’t be the only one for whom this statement jars. We may live in an age of emoting, but we should be able to see the difference between right and wrong.
“And it doesn’t feel right for a Home Office minister to put two police officers on a par with the thugs who killed them.”
Ms Turley told The Telegraph: “I’m dismayed that Nick Timothy would try and use a horrific situation that has deeply affected my community, and my local police force for a cheap political tweet. One that is deliberately disingenuous at that.
“The two officers who were killed are heroes whose bravery will never be forgotten, and that is not diminished by recognising seven lives were lost in this horrendous incident.”
![Pc Tom Clough and Pc Matthew Blades, officers from Cleveland Police, were killed in the crash](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/briefs/2026/08/25/TELEMMGLPICT000499447361_17876454780132_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqyuLFFzXshuGqnr8zPdDWXhbQKbwj1ZsnNMhuR7O6ySI.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
It is understood that Ms Turley was speaking purely in her capacity as the MP for Redcar. She said she had remained in contact with the local police throughout the investigation to offer her support.
Ms Turley posted the statement on Sunday morning, before the identities of the five joyriders had been confirmed by police. It had already been reported that the car that had hit the police vehicle had been travelling the wrong way on a dual carriageway.
As the row broke out on Monday evening, masked youths were seen flying balloons and setting off flares in memory of one of the joyriders.
Dozens of Matusiak’s family and friends gathered on a field in South Bank, Middlesbrough, to honour his life, a few hundred yards from the site of the collision.
Tributes for the five young men were also shared on social media, with many of their friends saying they “can’t believe it” and were “heartbroken” and “lost for words”.
Balloon releases have been announced in their memory on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday at different locations, including in South Bank, near where the collision occurred.
One message, dedicated to all five, said: “We all knew use [sic] and knew use [sic] had hearts of gold and most loyalist lads.”
Ms Turley was pictured at a silent prayer vigil held inside St John the Evangelist Church in Middlesbrough.
In a statement issued by Cleveland Police, Pc Blades’s wife called him “my beloved husband, my best friend, and the most devoted father to our two young boys”.
Since the crash, nine men and three women, aged between 19 and 61, have been detained, with some suspected of “participating in the activities of an organised crime group”, drug dealing and possessing firearms, Cleveland Police said.
Meanwhile, the Police Federation of England and Wales has accused young people of “baiting police officers” with dangerous driving.
![A balloon release in memory of Jakob Matusiak, took place at South Bank Field in Middlesbrough](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/briefs/2026/08/25/TELEMMGLPICT000499451922_17876454777780_trans_NvBQzQNjv4Bq7t4Eljyiy6iRMFuEKY2dXKlZlVGkFVrulHDGfmLMmms.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
Paul Williams, acting deputy national chairman for the Police Federation of England and Wales, told BBC Breakfast: “Every day we can identify now numerous examples of young people sensationalising dangerous driving.
“Not just dangerous driving, but baiting police officers who are out there to protect the public. It’s a real problem. It’s causing officers concern.
“They shouldn’t have to be going out and worrying about whether they’re going to return home from their shift or not. But on top of that, wondering if they’re going to be plastered all over social media.
“It’s absolutely unacceptable and social media platforms need to take some action.”
Four of the five young men in the car had previous criminal convictions and were believed to be associated with another car which had been seen ramming properties earlier that morning.
![Police officers at the scene of the fatal crash on the A66 near Middlesbrough](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/briefs/2026/08/25/TELEMMGLPICT000499135085_17876454887540_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqpVlberWd9EgFPZtcLiMQf0Rf_Wk3V23H2268P_XkPxc.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
The force said that, on the morning of the collision, it had received several reports of two vehicles being driven dangerously.
The first, believed to be a Volvo XC60, was witnessed ramming properties in the Middlesbrough area.
The second, a Volkswagen Passat, was believed to have been associated with the activities of the Volvo.
Police said both vehicles were operating with cloned number plates but were picked up by automated number plate recognition technology.
The Volvo XC60 involved in the initial reports has been traced and recovered in Middlesbrough.
Police said there was no evidence that filming of the activities on Friday night and Saturday morning was “for the purposes of TikTok”.
summary: Home Office minister and Redcar MP Anna Turley faced criticism from shadow justice secretary Nick Timothy for paying tribute to all seven victims of a fatal crash on the A66. The collision killed two police officers, Pc Matthew Blades and Pc Tom Clough, as well as five youths traveling the wrong way in a car linked to dangerous driving. Turley defended her statement, clarifying that she spoke as a local MP and emphasizing that recognizing the loss of seven lives does not diminish the heroism of the slain officers.
key_points: A Home Office minister and Redcar MP, Anna Turley, laid flowers and paid tribute to all seven individuals who died in a crash on the A66 near Middlesbrough.
The collision resulted in the deaths of two police officers, Pc Matthew Blades and Pc Tom Clough, and five youths driving a car in the wrong direction.
Shadow justice secretary Nick Timothy criticized Turley, arguing it was inappropriate for a Home Office minister to equate the two police officers with the young men in the crash.
Turley dismissed Timothy's remarks as a cheap political attack, stating she was acting as a local MP to address a tragedy affecting her community.
Four of the five deceased youths had previous criminal convictions, and police reported the incident followed earlier sightings of vehicles being driven dangerously in the area.

title: UK weather: Met Office issues yellow weather warnings for thunderstorms
author: Tomasz Schafernaker
content:
![Three women walk under an umbrella during a rainstorm in London](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/924/cpsprodpb/b1a4/live/ab342830-a061-11f1-a8b2-73da9d854f1b.png)
- Published
Yellow weather warnings have been issued by the Met Office as heavy rain and thunderstorms are forecast to break out over parts of the UK later this week.
The warnings span Wednesday and Thursday and include parts of east Wales, the Midlands, northern England, East Anglia and southern England - including London.
It is likely to be the one of the most widespread outbreaks of heavy rain across southern and central parts of the UK this summer.
While good news for regions plagued by drought, significant accumulations could lead to flash flooding where the ground is too dry and hard to absorb the downpours. Lightning, large hail and gusty winds are also possible.
Thunderstorms to fire up on Wednesday morning
The storms, which will drift out of France and move northwards, will be sparked as warm and humid air sets in from the south.
Initially, a few showers are likely to reach Cornwall and the West Country during Tuesday evening, but heavier downpours bringing thunder and lightning are likely to hit later in the night.
The first band of heavy showers may reach the southeast coast of England around midnight, and then cross Greater London before moving northwards into the home counties and East Anglia.
![A map depicting the area covered by a yellow weather warning, which includes Basingstoke and London in the south and Stockport and Sheffield in the north.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/a5a4/live/07794620-a067-11f1-aed2-8d6da8d75094.jpg)
The first yellow weather warning is set to come into force at 03:00 BST on Wednesday and last until 22:00 BST.
Though not all locations in the warning area will experience thunderstorms, flooding is possible in those that do, with 20-30mm of rain possible in less than an hour.
The hardest hit locations could see up to 40-50mm in two to three hours.
Flash flooding is possible in areas where the ground is dry and very hard, making it difficult for rainfall to be absorbed. The most intense downpours could also bring large hail with gusty winds.
During the morning on Wednesday, the storms may spread further north into the Midlands and the Peak District but the forecast becomes less certain in terms of location and intensity.
Thunderstorm and flood threat continues on Thursday
The storms and downpours which will have brought flash flooding and hail are forecast to continue into Thursday.
Some may become slow moving across the Midlands, Wales and Northern England leading to more flash flooding.
Many areas could see 20-30mm of rain in just three hours, with up to 50mm possible in some places.
According to the Met Office, there is also a small chance of considerably higher totals, particularly over east-facing higher ground, where more than 75mm could fall within 12 hours.
Lightning may be frequent and hail of around 1-2cm could fall.
Why are rain and thunderstorms difficult to forecast?
Thunderstorms are notoriously difficult to predict because they can develop very quickly and on a relatively small scale.
Tiny differences in temperature, humidity, wind and atmospheric instability can determine whether a storm forms at all or where it moves.
Forecast models can often identify the risk of thunderstorms across a wider area, but pinpointing precisely where and when an individual storm will strike is very hard.
Even a few kilometres can make the difference between a torrential downpour with thunder and lightning, and somewhere staying completely dry.
summary: The Met Office has issued yellow weather warnings for heavy rain and thunderstorms across parts of the UK for Wednesday and Thursday. The storms, moving northwards from France, threaten to bring flash flooding, lightning, large hail, and gusty winds, particularly where dry ground cannot absorb the rainfall. While thunderstorms are notoriously difficult to forecast precisely, some areas could see up to 40-50mm of rain in a few hours, with higher totals possible in certain locations.
key_points: Yellow weather warnings span Wednesday and Thursday across east Wales, the Midlands, northern England, East Anglia, and southern England, including London.
The storms are expected to bring 20-30mm of rain in under an hour, with some locations potentially seeing up to 40-50mm in two to three hours.
Hard and dry ground creates a risk of flash flooding because it cannot easily absorb the heavy downpours.
Severe weather hazards may also include frequent lightning, large hail, and gusty winds.
Thunderstorms are difficult to predict on a small scale due to tiny differences in temperature, humidity, wind, and atmospheric instability.

title: Government lays out housing plans but Burnham backtracks on social renting pledge – UK politics live
author: Tom Ambrose
content:
Minister rejects accusation Burnham broke promise on council homes funding
A housing minister has rejected suggestions that Andy Burnham has failed to his keep promises on council housing, as the government unveiled a nearly £10bn plan to boost “genuinely affordable homes”.
The prime minister has pledged to carry out the biggest council housebuilding programme since the postwar period, with more than 70,000 homes, 60% allocated for social rent, to be delivered across England.
However, Burnham has faced accusation of watering down his ambitions after he previously called for the entire £39bn social and affordable homes programme to be spent on council housing.
Asked whether he accepted that Burnham had failed to keep promises made in the lead-up to the byelection, housing minister Matthew Pennycook told BBC Breakfast:
No, I don’t. I mean, Andy Burnham said in the byelection that he wanted to see more money spent on social rent on council housebuilding.
That’s exactly what we’re doing through this initial wave of funding.
Government lays out housing plans but Burnham backtracks on social renting pledge
Good morning and welcome to the UK politics live blog.
The government has set out its plans to spend an initial £10bn on a mix of subsidised housing in England, with a target of 60% being social renting.
The funding, which comes from the 10-year Affordable Homes Programme, is in line with the Starmer government’s policy and sees Andy Burnham backtrack on his proposal to rip up housing plans and boost social home building.
Burnham previously called for the programme to be spent entirely on social homes, which are more heavily subsidised and therefore more affordable than other types of government-funded housing.
There’s £39bn allocated over a 10-year period … I’m saying that should be dedicated to council homes. Let’s not be coy any more … I’m saying council homes because control matters.
Under the plans announced on Monday, however, £10bn will be spent helping to build 70,000 homes outside London, about 60% of which will be social rented houses. The rest will be other types of accommodation such as shared ownership schemes and sheltered housing.
London will get another £6bn, which will be allocated at a later date.
Ministers said the investment would help bring the government closer to its promise of building 300,000 affordable homes over the next 10 years. It will be spent by 33 “strategic partners”, who will be guaranteed funding for the next decade to help deliver their plans.
The Guardian has learned that for the first time in the history of the scheme, three of those partners will be local councils, as the government looks to deliver what Burnham has promised will be “the biggest council housebuilding programme since the postwar period”.
Andy Burnham has said he plans to travel to the US next month to join European leaders lobbying Donald Trump to supply Ukraine with Patriot missiles. The UK prime minister told Bloomberg he was “looking forward to going to New York” in September, which is when the UN general assembly will meet. He said details of the trip were not “fully confirmed” but it was “likely” to go ahead.
AI models trained on Ukrainian battlefield data will be used to stop protesters and foreign states targeting UK defence sites, railways and energy plants under a deal struck between London and Kyiv. Private companies will also be given access to the vast trove of data from Ukraine’s Avengers AI lab to help build new systems, the first agreement of its kind in the UK.
Social housing tenants will be evicted if they fail to keep their gardens well maintained under a Reform UK government, the party has announced. Lee Anderson, the party’s chair, said that if Reform came to power it would insist that those in social rented homes would be required to keep their properties decorated and gardens looked after.
